summary: Source-anchored research for Transaction Anti-Patterns. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: When a consistency invariant can be enforced within one document, prefer a schema and atomic single-document write that enforce it; MongoDB documents that single-document operations are atomic and that embedding can remove the need for multi-document transactions in many use cases. Use a transaction when the invariant actually spans documents. (high confidence)

Keep transactions short and size-bounded. Long-running or oversized transactions retain old snapshot state and uncommitted changes, which can pressure WiredTiger's cache, raise latency for other operations, and cause rollback or abort. Avoid large batches in one transaction and abort abandoned work promptly. (high confidence)

Keep DDL such as index creation or collection renames outside the transaction's critical path when they touch the same namespace. MongoDB documents that pending DDL can wait for an active transaction, while new affected transactions can wait behind the pending DDL and then abort on lock timeout. (high confidence)

Make retryable transaction callbacks idempotent and do not perform irreversible external side effects inside them unless those effects use deduplication. A driver's `withTransaction` callback may run multiple times when a transient transaction error causes the whole transaction to be retried, so an email, charge, or webhook in the callback can otherwise happen more than once. (high confidence)

For integrations that start transactions lazily, avoid sending multiple asynchronous commands on the same session before its first transaction command completes. A Payload issue reports that out-of-order first commands can fail with `NoSuchTransaction` on its tested stack. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13)

Abort a transaction you abandon, and abort and retry a transaction when an individual operation errors, to prevent storage cache pressure from hurting performance. WiredTiger keeps older committed versions in a history store to serve long-running transactions, and when the oldest transaction or timestamp cannot move forward, history must be held in cache. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-production-consideration.md ; https://source.wiredtiger.com/10.0.0/arch-hs.html ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/WT-4107

An uncommitted transaction that puts excessive pressure on the WiredTiger cache aborts with a write conflict error, and a transaction too large to ever fit in the cache aborts with TransactionTooLargeForCache. Starting in MongoDB 6.2, the server does not retry a transaction that receives a TransactionTooLargeForCache error, because the cache is too small and a retry is likely to fail. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-in-applications.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-production-consideration.md

A TransientTransactionError can cause the entire transaction to be retried, which invokes the callback again; write-conflict TransientTransactionErrors are expected to be a common cause of retry loops. Sources: https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/transactions-convenient-api/transactions-convenient-api/

Pass the `ClientSession` to every database operation that should participate in `withTransaction`. The helper does not enforce this association, so an operation without the session can run outside the transaction. (high confidence)
